task: What guidance did Nike give for the current quarter on its most recent earnings call, and how did the stock react?

key.question: Which is Nike's most recent earnings call, and did it give explicit guidance for the current quarter (Q2 FY27, Sept–Nov 2026)?
key.answer: The latest call was for Q1 FY27 (quarter ended Aug 31, 2026), held Oct 1, 2026. Nike gave no full numeric Q2 revenue or EPS guidance. An analyst pointed this out on the call, and CFO Dave Friend declined to give a Q2 number. The only Q2-specific guidance was qualitative: roughly 400 bps of revenue headwind from lapping Cyber Week promotions in EMEA and a high North America sell-in comparison. He also said growth rates would be pressured sequentially in Q2. Nike's next report (Q2 FY27) is expected in December 2026, so check the date.

key.question: What full-year FY27 guidance did Nike give?
key.answer: Revenue is expected to decline by a high-single-digit percentage in FY27. EBIT is expected to fall by more than revenue, on gross margin pressure, fixed-cost deleverage and higher input costs, partly offset by SG&A that stays down year over year. Nike will not give gross margin guidance. Greater China revenue is assumed to get worse for the rest of the year. Reports put the adjusted EPS range at $1.15–$1.35 and the midpoint about 22% below the $1.61 consensus; the EPS range is from secondary sources and I did not check it against the call transcript. Since Q1 revenue was down 4%, the outlook implies much steeper declines in Q2–Q4.

key.question: What were the Q1 FY27 results that framed the guidance?
key.answer: Revenue was $11.2B (-4% reported, -5% currency-neutral). Reports put it slightly below the $11.3B consensus, but management said it was within its guided range. Gross margin was 42.8%, up 60 bps. EPS was $0.48 (net income $712M), versus about $0.43–0.44 consensus and $0.49 a year earlier. Greater China fell 26%, EMEA fell 5%, APLA was flat and North America rose 2%. Nike Sportswear was down low double digits, with Dunk revenue cut by almost 50%. Nike Performance was up high single digits.

key.question: How did the stock react?
key.answer: Shares fell in extended trading on Oct 1, 2026. Early reports showed about 3-4%, and later reports showed roughly 5-9% (Reuters reported 8.5%, TIKR about 9%). On Oct 2 they fell as much as 5.3% intraday to about $33.29, after a prior close of $35.15 (low $31.97). Volume was roughly 57.6M shares, about twice the average. One aggregator shows an Oct 2 close of about $33.87 (-3.6%), so the exact close is uncertain. The shares were near the bottom of a 52-week range of $31.97–$74.78.

key_original.answer: Shares fell about 3% in extended trading on Oct 1, 2026. On Oct 2 they fell as much as 5.3% intraday to about $33.29, after a prior close of $35.15 (low $31.97). Volume was roughly 57.6M shares, about twice the average. One aggregator shows an Oct 2 close of about $33.87 (-3.6%), so the exact close is uncertain. The shares were near the bottom of a 52-week range of $31.97–$74.78.

audit.why: The after-hours move was reported at different sizes depending on the time of the snapshot. Benzinga Pro showed -4.17% at $33.64, one aggregator showed about -5.5% at $33.20, and TIKR (updated Oct 2) said about 9%. Reuters, per Answer A, said 8.5%. I could not open the Reuters page, so that figure is unconfirmed. The next-day regular session is better documented. The vermoegenszentrum page says Nike fell 5.28% to $33.29 on Oct 2 from a $35.15 close. The intraday low was $31.97, volume was about 57.6M against a 27.55M average, and the 52-week range was $31.97–$74.78. The key's Oct 2 figures match that page. The key's "about 3%" after-hours figure is one early snapshot, and an after-hours drop of 3% to 9% is defensible depending on timing. I did not verify the key's aggregator close of about $33.87 (-3.6%).
audit.disputed_point: Size of the after-hours drop on Oct 1, 2026: the key says about 3%, Answer A says 8.5% (Reuters).

key.question: What strategic or cost actions were announced alongside the guidance?
key.answer: Nike announced the multiyear 'Pace' productivity program, targeting about $2.5B in savings against roughly $1B in implementation costs. It will reorganize into three geographies (Americas, APGC, EMEA) from FY28. It will also continue to cut supply into the marketplace, which pressures reported revenue through the rest of FY27 and into FY28. Nike is cleaning up China digital distribution to the official flagship storefronts on Tmall, JD and Douyin.

key.question: What are the key risks and uncertainties for someone acting on this today (Nov 10, 2026)?
key.answer: Nike gave no numeric Q2 guide, so the Q2 expectations in use are analyst inference from the full-year range and the 400 bps headwind. Greater China is assumed to keep deteriorating, and Sportswear/Jordan are weak. The stock moved after Oct 2, and I did not check today's price. The EPS range and the close figures come from secondary sources and should be verified against the Nike press release and 8-K.
